memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"After Moses had gone down the mountain to the people, he consecrated them, and
they washed their clothes. Then he said to the people, 'Prepare yourselves for
the third day. Abstain from sexual relations.'" - Ex 19:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The preparation is carried out. Clothes washed, people set apart, and a temporary
abstaining from marital relations.

That last instruction needs care. It is not a suggestion that marriage or sex is
impure. Scripture is clear that marriage is honourable and the marriage bed is
undefiled (Heb 13:4), and God Himself established it in Eden before any sin
entered the world.

This was a temporary setting-aside of something good for the sake of undivided
focus. Paul mentions something similar for married Christians: a mutual, agreed,
temporary abstaining "so that you may devote yourselves to prayer," followed by
coming together again (1 Cor 7:5). Notice how carefully Paul guards it, by mutual
consent and for a limited time.

The principle is not that ordinary life is unclean. It is that there are moments
worth clearing space for.

Most of us know this instinctively in other areas. We put the phone away for an
important conversation. We clear the diary for a family occasion. Setting
something aside is how we signal that this matters more.

Three days of deliberate focus, because God was coming.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What good thing might you set aside temporarily to make room for God?
2. Does anything in your life get the focus you would give to a once-in-a-
   lifetime occasion?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to clear space for You rather than fitting You into whatever is
left over. Amen.
